kind: Published NASA aggregate summaries; not astronaut-level records or a fitted training dataset

observations.label: Bone density lost per month
observations.context: NASA reports this broad average for four-to-six-month missions. It is not a separate estimate for each bone or exercise routine.
observations.model_use: Historical context only. Active hip/back rates now reference site-specific human study measurements.

observations.label: Average strength and cardio fitness loss
observations.context: NASA summarizes ISS mission data. Outcomes vary by person and measurement. This is a post-mission change, not a monthly rate or a muscle-mass measurement.
observations.model_use: Reference only. Not used to fit daily muscle or cardio rates; mission length and individual records are unavailable in this summary.

exercise_context.note: NASA describes crews averaging about two hours of daily exercise. Our equal strength/cardio split and shorter routine are illustrative choices, not an astronaut prescription. A separate NASA risk summary describes 1.5 hours of training six to seven days per week; these accounts are not a single standardized protocol.

open_data_roadmap.label: NASA OSDR OSD-489
open_data_roadmap.title: Quantifying Cancellous Bone Structural Changes in Microgravity: Axial Skeleton Results from the RR-1 Mission
open_data_roadmap.context: Rodent Research-1 (SpaceX CRS-4): female C57BL/6J mice spent 37 days on the ISS; lumbar vertebra micro-CT, flight versus ground controls.
open_data_roadmap.model_use: Identified, not imported. Planned use: cross-species check of the shape of early trabecular bone loss. Mouse results do not set human rates.

open_data_roadmap.label: NASA Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA)
open_data_roadmap.title: Individual astronaut measurements on request
open_data_roadmap.context: Individual crew bone, muscle and fitness records are held under NASA's data-request process.
open_data_roadmap.model_use: Not requested. Required before any per-person accuracy claim or fitted personal factors.
